record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: For a closed smooth manifold M of even dimension 2m, how is the sign of the Euler characteristic constrained by asphericity or sectional curvature? More precisely, if M is aspherical, must (-1)^m χ(M) ≥ 0? If M carries a Riemannian metric, must one have (-1)^m χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) < 0, (-1)^m χ(M) ≥ 0 when sec(M) ≤ 0, χ(M) = 0 when sec(M) = 0, χ(M) ≥ 0 when sec(M) ≥ 0, and χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) > 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 (Hopf Conjecture). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of even dimension dim(M) = 2m, then (−1)m · χ(M) ≥ 0. If M is a closed smooth manifold of even dimension dim(M) = 2m with Riemannian metric and with sectional curvature sec(M), then (−1)m · χ(M) > 0 if sec(M) < 0; (−1)m · χ(M) ≥ 0 if sec(M) ≤ 0; χ(M) = 0 if sec(M) = 0; χ(M) ≥ 0 if sec(M) ≥ 0; χ(M) > 0 if sec(M) > 0.

artifact.status_search_result: The Hopf conjectures on the sign of the Euler characteristic of closed even-dimensional manifolds with definite sectional curvature, and the related conjecture for aspherical manifolds, remain open in general. They are confirmed in dimensions 2 and 4 (via Gauss-Bonnet and Chern-Milnor type arguments), and partial results exist (e.g., for Kähler manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature, and Davis-Okun's results in low dimensions), but the general statements are unresolved as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Hopf conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjectures remain open in general; known in low dimensions and special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The Hopf conjectures on sign of Euler characteristic under curvature/asphericity assumptions are still open.
